AXP.rationale: AXP presents a moderately attractive fundamental picture with a strong franchise offset by a material cash-flow deterioration. Pillar 1: Earnings trajectory is solid — YoY EPS growth of +17.6% on +9.3% revenue growth, 33% ROE, 26.6% net margin, and Q1 2026 billed business growth of +10% YoY (fastest pace in 3 years). The closed-loop network moat is intact with 73% of new accounts being fee-paying products and record net card fees of $10B (+18% YoY). However, operating cash flow has declined for three consecutive quarters (−20.2% YoY, −39.0% QoQ in Q1 2026), creating an earnings-quality concern, and debt has risen 14.6% YoY to $58.75B with debt/equity at 1.728x. Pillar 2: Valuation is cheap vs own history — trailing P/E of 19.1x sits at the floor of the 12-month range (18.4–25.3x), roughly 15% below the midpoint, and P/B at 6.3x is near the bottom of its 6.1–8.2x range. The earnings yield of 5.2% exceeds the 10-year Treasury at 4.47% by 73bps. Pillar 3: Management reaffirmed FY26 guidance of revenue growth 9–10% and EPS $17.30–$17.90, and a 16% dividend increase was announced alongside Q1 results. The Fanatics partnership (June 4) extends the rewards ecosystem. These are modest positive catalysts but not strong enough to materially shift the score. Net: the franchise quality and valuation discount support a mildly-to-moderately attractive rating, but the cash-flow deterioration and rising leverage prevent a higher conviction call. Score of +0.25 reflects the tension between a strong business at a cheap valuation and a genuine cash-conversion concern.
